title: Model 8 (Ensemble Bagging)
text:
The decision tree saw some improvement to the predicted RMSE. An ensemble model is next to be tried.

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor

data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')
X = pd.get_dummies(data.drop(['customer_id', 'monthly_spend'], axis=1), drop_first=True).fillna(-1)

model = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=100, n_jobs = -1, oob_score = True, max_depth=10, random_state=617)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')

title: Model 12 (SVR)
text:
An attempt at using support vector machines. Interestingly this turned out to be the worst performing model.

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.svm import SVR
from sklearn.metrics import root_mean_squared_error

# Read data
data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')

X_raw = pd.get_dummies(data.drop(['customer_id', 'monthly_spend'], axis = 1), drop_first=True).fillna(0)
y = data['monthly_spend']
X_train_raw, X_test_raw, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(X_raw, y, test_size=0.3, random_state=617)
scale = StandardScaler()
scale.fit(X_train_raw)
X_train = scale.transform(X_train_raw)
X_test = scale.transform(X_test_raw)

model = SVR(kernel = 'rbf', C = 1, gamma=0.1) 
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')
scoring_X_raw = pd.get_dummies(scoring_data.drop(['customer_id'], axis=1), drop_first=True).fillna(0)

scoring_X_raw = scoring_X_raw.reindex(columns=X_raw.columns, fill_value=0)
scoring_X_scaled = scale.transform(scoring_X_raw)

final_predictions = model.predict(scoring_X_scaled)

# Construct submission
submission_file = pd.DataFrame({'customer_id': scoring_data.customer_id, 'monthly_spend': final_predictions})
submission_file.to_csv('../PACFiles/submission_file_13.csv', index=False)

pred_train = model.predict(X_train)
pred_test = model.predict(X_test)
rmse_train = root_mean_squared_error(y_train, pred_train)
rmse_test = root_mean_squared_error(y_test, pred_test)
print("Training RMSE:", rmse_train)
print("Testing RMSE:", rmse_test)

Training RMSE: 475.6199733835682
Testing RMSE: 480.82217671768217

title: Model 6 (Feature Selection)
text:
It now feels like time to focus in on suspected high impact variables, including annual_income, avg_transaction_value, num_transactions, and credit_score. I also again included the invented income_interaction variable.

import pandas as pd
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression

data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/analysis_data.csv')
features = ['annual_income', 'avg_transaction_value', 'num_transactions',

X = data[features].fillna(data[features].median())
X['income_interaction'] = X['num_transactions'] * X['avg_transaction_value']

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')

submission_file = pd.DataFrame({'customer_id': scoring_data.customer_id, 'monthly_spend': pred})

title: Best Model (Optimized Ensemble)
text:
An ensemble model was used in this case, as well as in a few previous models. On the scikit learn website, I found HistGradientBoostingRegressor, an alternative to GradientBoostingRegressor that they claim is “orders of magnitude faster” when the number of samples is large. In this specific model, the learning_rate is reduced and max_iter is increased to refine the model’s accuracy. In previous models I experimented with including only certain variables, and some of those models did see an improvement because of it. However, in this model I found that including all variables consistently led to better results.
I used the data itself to predict a rough RMSE, which in almost every model did end up aligning closely with the PAC scores. This helped with making minor adjustments to each model to hopefully be able to provide a submission that would perform well in the competition. This optimized ensemble model proved to be the best of my models both in the public and private scores.

model.fit(X,y)

scoring_data = pd.read_csv('../PACFiles/scoring_data.csv')
scoring_X = pd.get_dummies(scoring_data.drop(['customer_id'], axis=1), drop_first=True)

train_pred = model.predict(X)
